overall: Atlanta is having a warmer-than-expected afternoon, with the temperature already reaching 84.2°F as of 14:00 ET — well above the NWS forecast high of ~83°F and surpassing all NWP model forecasts (ECMWF 82.3, HRRR 82.6, NBM 82.6). The sky is partly cloudy (SCT, ~38% cloud fraction) with a brisk NW wind around 17 mph, which may limit further significant warming but hasn't prevented the day from trending hotter than models anticipated. The active flood warnings are for the Satilla River in far southeast Georgia and are irrelevant to Atlanta's temperature today.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF, HRRR, NBM) clustered tightly around 82.3–82.6°F, yet observed temperatures have already blown past that range by nearly 2°F, indicating a notable model cold bias today. The intraday momentum is still slightly positive (+1.8°F/hr velocity, +1.286°F/hr² acceleration at 14:00), though the predicted peak hour of ~13.9h (≈13:54 ET) is essentially now, suggesting the bulk of daytime heating is complete.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max already at 84.2°F and mild positive velocity persisting right at the predicted peak window, the day's high will almost certainly exceed 84°F and likely squeeze out a few more tenths to low-to-mid 85s before cooling begins in earnest. The META model's distribution is heavily concentrated in the 84–85°F bucket (46.1%) with meaningful probability in 86–87°F (29.5%), and the floor is locked at 84.2°F by current observations. Confidence is moderate-high that the final TMAX lands near 85–85.5°F, with the main upside risk being the still-positive velocity and the main downside risk being the strengthening NW winds accelerating the afternoon cool-down.
